# Google解释了如何出现在AI搜索中：基础SEO与查询扩展

作者：@dylandgtl  
日期：2026-11-01（北京时间）  
来源：[X原帖](https://x.com/dylandgtl/status/2116685283286773794)  
分类：方法

## 中文全文

过去一年里，企业主不断被告知，自己需要一套全新的 AI 搜索策略。GEO、AEO、LLM SEO、AI SEO——标签一直在变，推销话术也跟着变。

Google 现在直接回应了这个问题。在一篇名为《Good SEO is good GEO》的文章中，Google 的 Brendon Kraham 解释了它的 AI 功能如何选择展示内容。答案没有行业渲染得那么戏剧化，但确实会影响你应该如何投资自己的网站。

## AI 搜索与普通搜索建立在相同的基础上

Google 表示，它的生成式 AI 功能与传统搜索使用相同的核心排名和质量系统。AI Overviews 与 AI Mode 从 Google 现有搜索索引中获取当前信息。

实际含义是：如果 Google 无法抓取、理解和信任你的网站，你同样不会出现在 AI 回答里。没有旁门捷径。

## Google 说你不需要什么

这份指南反对当前正在被推销的几种捷径：

- 为机器人而不是人写的别扭内容。

- 散布在页面各处、人为设计的“摘要诱饵”。

- 专门为 Google 搜索准备的 AI 文本文件。

- 在各种不相干网站上铺设的低质量提及。

最后一点很重要。Google 的 AI 可以利用全网信息，包括博客、视频和论坛讨论。在一个没人看的页面上付费获得提及，与真实评价、本地媒体报道或可信刊物中的专家引述，并不是一回事。更多提及并不自动意味着更多可见性。

## Google 说真正有效的是什么

这些建议并不陌生：

- 发布新鲜、有用的内容。

- 提供原创贡献，而不是到处都能找到的内容。

- 展示真正的专业能力。

- 让网站保持快速、易用。

- 确保企业信息在所有出现的地方都准确无误。

对本地企业来说，最后一点意味着做好 **Google Business Profile（Google 商家资料）**。营业时间、服务、照片、类别和评价，都会成为 Google 使用的信息。Google 也指出，可以通过 **Search Console** 查看这些工作是否转化为可见性。

## 大多数人会忽略的部分：查询扩展（Query Fan-Out）

这正是 AI 搜索不同的地方。

传统搜索通常只有一次查询。而 AI Mode 中的一个详细问题，可能会在后台围绕相关子主题触发多次搜索。Google 将其称为 query fan-out。

想象一位潜在客户问：“附近哪家医美机构最适合为深色皮肤做激光脱毛，我需要做几次？”

为了回答这个问题，Google 可能会寻找以下信息：

- 你所在城市的激光脱毛服务。

- 哪些激光适合较深肤色。

- 通常需要的治疗次数。

- 价格或咨询详情。

- 副作用和恢复情况。

- 提到这些具体效果的评价。

一个泛泛的“激光脱毛”页面，大概覆盖不了所有这些内容。如果一家诊所能清楚、详细地回答每一个问题，就给了 Google 更多找到并引用它的机会。

## “好的 SEO 就是好的 GEO”，不意味着继续做内容单薄的 SEO

基础没有变。改变的是内容深度的重要程度。

每项服务只有一个简短页面、文案套模板、没有 FAQ，这样的网站原本就表现不佳。在 AI 搜索中，这种差距会进一步扩大。能够出现的企业，是那些能回答客户预约前全部问题的企业：适合谁、预期过程怎样、效果持续多久、开始需要多少钱、服务商为什么具备资质，以及真实客户怎么说。

## 下一步做什么

- **审计服务页面。**每个页面是否回答了客户打电话之前会问的问题？如果没有，就补充完善。

- **扩展配套内容。**围绕最赚钱的服务，增加 FAQ、治疗比较、术后护理指南，以及说明适用人群的页面。

- **整理 Google 商家资料。**确认服务、类别、营业时间和照片均为最新，并持续获得真实评价。

- **争取可信的提及。**本地媒体、行业协会和合作企业，比批量目录收录更有分量。

- **检查技术基础。**确保网站可以被索引，在移动端加载迅速，并有清晰的标题层级。

- **关注 Search Console。**跟踪哪些页面获得展示，以及哪些查询正在增长。

## 总结

叫它 SEO、GEO，还是 AI SEO，标签并不重要。如果希望出现在 AI 搜索中，就建设一个 Google 能够抓取、理解、信任，并能在有人询问你所提供的产品或服务时，有把握推荐的网站。

## 外文原文

For the past year, business owners have been told they need a whole new strategy for AI search. GEO, AEO, LLM SEO, AI SEO. The labels keep changing, and so do the sales pitches.

Google has now addressed this directly. In a piece titled “Good SEO is good GEO,” Google’s Brendon Kraham explained how its AI features choose what to show. The answer is less dramatic than the industry has made it sound, but it does change how you should be investing in your website.

AI Search Runs on the Same Foundation as Regular Search

Google says its generative AI features use the same core ranking and quality systems as traditional Search. AI Overviews and AI Mode pull current information from Google’s existing search index.

In practical terms, if Google can’t crawl your site, understand it, and trust it, you won’t show up in AI answers either. There is no side door.

What Google Says You Don’t Need

The guidance pushes back on several shortcuts being sold right now:

- Content written awkwardly for bots instead of people

- Artificial “snippet bait” scattered across pages

- Special AI text files for Google Search

- Low-quality mentions spread across random websites

That last point matters. Google’s AI can draw on information from across the web, including blogs, videos and forum discussions. A paid mention on a page nobody reads is not the same as a real review, local press coverage, or an expert quoted in a trusted publication. More mentions does not automatically mean more visibility.

What Google Says Actually Works

The recommendations are familiar:

- Publish fresh, useful content

- Contribute something original that isn’t available everywhere else

- Show real expertise

- Keep your website fast and easy to use

- Keep your business information accurate everywhere it appears

For local businesses, that last point means your **Google Business Profile**. Your hours, services, photos, categories and reviews all feed the information Google uses. Google also points to **Search Console** as the way to see whether your work is translating into visibility.

The Part Most People Will Miss: Query Fan-Out

This is where AI search is different.

A traditional search is usually one query. A detailed question in AI Mode can trigger several searches behind the scenes across related subtopics. Google calls this query fan-out.

Picture a potential client asking: “What’s the best med spa near me for laser hair removal on darker skin, and how many sessions will I need?”

To answer that, Google may look for information on:

- Laser hair removal in your city

- Which lasers are suitable for darker skin tones

- Typical number of sessions

- Pricing or consultation details

- Side effects and recovery

- Reviews mentioning those specific results

A single generic “Laser Hair Removal” page probably won’t cover all of that. A clinic with clear, detailed answers to each of those questions gives Google more chances to find it and cite it.

“Good SEO Is Good GEO” Doesn’t Mean “Keep Doing Thin SEO”

The fundamentals haven’t changed. What has changed is how much depth matters.

A website with one short page per service, stock copy and no FAQs was already underperforming. In AI search, that gap gets wider. The businesses that show up will be the ones that answer the full set of questions a customer has before booking: who it’s for, what to expect, how long results last, what it costs to get started, what makes the provider qualified, and what real clients say.

What to Do Next

- **Audit your service pages.** Does each one answer the questions customers ask before they call? If not, expand it.

- **Build out supporting content.** Add FAQs, treatment comparisons, aftercare guides and candidate pages around your most profitable services.

- **Clean up your Google Business Profile.** Confirm services, categories, hours and photos are current, and keep generating real reviews.

- **Earn credible mentions.** Local media, industry associations and partner businesses carry far more weight than bulk directory listings.

- **Check the technical basics.** Make sure your site is indexable, loads quickly on mobile and has a clear heading structure.

- **Watch Search Console.** Track which pages earn impressions and which queries are growing.

The Bottom Line

Call it SEO, GEO or AI SEO. The label doesn’t matter. If you want to appear in AI search, build a website Google can crawl, understand, trust and confidently recommend when someone asks a question about what you offer.
